Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 6 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these; the test file is new):
  server/pipeline/loop_runner.py
  tests/test_world_assets_exposure.py

THE GAP, measured minutes ago on the live system. The weekly drumbeat planner
(promo_schedule.plan_weekly_drumbeat, already merged and tested) ran a real tick and
planned promotion touches for four published episodes — then skipped EVERY one with
reason asset_missing, and the skip list named episodes as "episode-15", "episode-4":
placeholder ids. Two causes, both in loop_runner.assemble_world:
  1. The world's episode records do not carry the episode's DIRECTORY NAME as a stable
     id, so downstream consumers fall back to index-based placeholders (the queue's
     stalled list printed ids as null for the same reason earlier today).
  2. The records carry nothing about what promotional assets exist on disk, so the
     honest planner (it refuses to invent assets) correctly reports asset_missing for
     episodes that HAVE three clips, a social image, and three social drafts sitting in
     their directories.
The planner is right; the world is starving it. Feed the world; do not touch the planner.

THE FIX, in server/pipeline/loop_runner.py only:
1. READ promo_schedule.plan_weekly_drumbeat and loop_tick's drumbeat call FIRST to learn
   the exact record keys the planner consumes for id, publish state, and assets. Match
   THOSE keys — do not invent a parallel vocabulary and do not edit the planner.
2. In assemble_world, each episode record must additionally carry:
   * the stable id: the episode DIRECTORY NAME (this is the repo-wide episode_id used by
     the DAG projection and the queue);
   * an assets summary scanned from the episode directory, shaped how the planner reads
     it, derived from what actually exists: clips/*.mp4 (names, sorted), social-image.png
     (bool or name), content/social-drafts/*.md (names, sorted). Scanning must be
     deterministic, tolerate a missing subdirectory (empty, never raise), and must NOT
     read file contents — names and existence only.
3. Do not change any other world key, the function signature, load_errors semantics, or
   the candidates/referrals feed merged earlier today.

TESTS (tests/test_world_assets_exposure.py; at least 6, tmp episode dirs):
 (1) THE GAP CLOSED, end to end: a tmp episodes dir with one published back-catalog
     episode carrying a clip file, a social image, and a social draft -> assemble_world
     -> loop_tick.plan_tick plans at least one promotion action whose episode id is the
     REAL directory name and whose asset names a REAL file — this test fails on
     yesterday's code;
 (2) episode records carry the directory name as their id (assert directly);
 (3) NEGATIVE: an episode with no assets still yields asset_missing in the plan's
     skipped list — the fix must not weaken the planner's refusal to invent;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a missing clips/ or social-drafts/ subdirectory yields empty asset lists
     and no exception;
 (5) determinism: identical dirs -> identical records including asset order;
 (6) the assets scan never appears for non-episode directories (no episode.json ->
     skipped as before);
 (7) NEGATIVE: unreadable episode.json still lands in load_errors exactly as before
     (no regression on the fail-visible path).
Keep tests/test_candidate_feed_wiring.py, tests/test_weekly_drumbeat.py,
tests/test_loop_runner.py, tests/test_loop_tick.py green.
